title: Realize R437 large-divisor Count guards with explicit binary tape arithmetic
body:
The R437 batched quotient caller previously delegated division by large family, GL and high factors to host-sized arithmetic. This package realizes those divisions and the high factor construction with fixed binary tape roles, preserving the unchanged nested quotient body's three exactness guards and restoration behavior.

The proof charges divisor setup, scans, moves, subtraction, normalization, borrowed-head restoration and scratch erasure. It supplies explicit uniform bounds for division, multiplication and radix power construction; the production parameter invoice is symbolic and very large. This is a scoped arithmetic/source-composition result, not a complete physical caller tariff or a new multiplication bound. Supplied constant tapes matching the compiled constants, Context/codebook preparation, and the inherited Word radix loop remain separate obligations.

Validation: 7,936 exhaustive divisions plus 12 wider cases, 1,024 multiplications, 18 powers, nine small executions of the original quotient body, all three factor rejection guards, malformed/alias controls, and five arithmetic/cleanup omission mutants. Registered Python 3.12 normal and optimized replay pass. Commit-byte/source-history checks and the official 16-file export pass; Git-free cold normal/optimized replay and actual source/typed-receipt corruption controls pass. Independent AI peer review additionally exercised 131/66-bit and 513/256-bit divisions and restoration/guard boundaries without finding a blocker. No production-size fixture was executed.

Reproduce: `/opt/homebrew/bin/python3.12 scripts/research_package.py --package research/r437-binary-divisor-realization`.

Claim: https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/4682#discussioncomment-19141163
